root_cause.text: `inode_switch_wbs_work_fn()` in the writeback subsystem could leave `wb->switch_work` pending while `wb->switch_wbs_ctxs` was empty because it re-queued/processsed items in a loop, allowing the `wb` object to lose its last `isw`-held reference and be freed before the work executed, resulting in a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `while (1)` loop and changes `inode_switch_wbs_work_fn()` to call `llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs)` once, with a new `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list)` comment explicitly stating that an empty list would be a problem because “references held by isw items protect wb from freeing”; the CVE text also says the loop allowed `wb->switch_work` to remain pending while `wb->switch_wbs_ctxs` was empty, causing `wb` to be freed while work was still pending.

intent_record.what: In inode_switch_wbs_work_fn(), the code now calls llist_del_all(&new_wb->switch_wbs_ctxs) once at the start, checks the result with WARN_ON_ONCE(!list) and returns early if it is empty, then performs wb_get(new_wb), a single synchronize_rcu(), and one llist_for_each_entry_safe() pass over the retrieved list. The նախկին loop that repeatedly re-queried the list, conditionally broke on empty, and synchronized RCU on each iteration was removed.
intent_record.how: The worker now processes all pending switch_wbs contexts in one batch instead of looping until the list drains. This preserves the intended RCU grace-period ordering before processing, while also flagging the unexpected case where the work runs with no queued contexts, which could indicate a logic error in reference handling or work scheduling.
